items.title: Swiss watchmakers face a price-and-value reality check.
items.summary: Deloitte’s survey of 6,500 consumers across 13 markets suggests buyers put price-to-value ahead of the industry’s constant flow of novelties. It also highlights a growing mismatch between brands’ focus on mono-brand boutiques and customers’ preference for choice and comparison.

items.title: Bangkok Watch Week signals Southeast Asia’s growing horological pull.
items.summary: The second Siam Paragon Bangkok Watch Week will run September 22–27 with more than 45 participating brands—more than double the first edition. Its growth shows how watch fairs are increasingly reaching toward collector communities beyond the traditional European circuit.

items.title: A. Lange & Söhne pairs new complications with the world of classic cars.
items.summary: At Hampton Court Palace’s Concours of Elegance, Lange presented the new platinum Triple Split and two 1815 Up/Down special editions. For a small high-watchmaking house, the event shows how cultural settings can frame craft and heritage more effectively than a standalone launch.

items.title: WatchPro USA names the people and businesses shaping the American watch market.
items.summary: The 2026 WatchPro USA Awards recognised achievement across retail, brand building, customer experience and industry leadership—not merely new releases. Its winners offer a useful snapshot of the businesses and people setting the pace in a growing American watch market.

items.title: Jaeger-LeCoultre brings fifteen complications into one Grande Sonnerie.
items.summary: Jaeger-LeCoultre’s one-off Duomètre Grande Complication à Grande Sonnerie unites a Westminster-style grande sonnerie, minute repeater, perpetual calendar and flying tourbillon in Calibre 182. It is a forceful reminder that extreme mechanical watchmaking remains central to the maison’s identity.

items.title: Panerai marks a century in Florence with an eight-day Luminor.
items.summary: For the centenary of its historic Florence boutique, Panerai revisits a 1960s reference in the limited Luminor Firenze 8 Giorni PAM01794. The release uses the brand’s familiar eight-day hand-wound movement to connect its modern identity with its Florentine origins.

items.title: Gérald Genta returns to the minute repeater with restraint.
items.summary: The revived maison’s Geneva Minute Repeater Golden Obsidian pairs a 40mm yellow-gold cushion case with a natural golden-obsidian dial, at roughly 9.6mm thick. It continues the LVMH-backed revival through thin dress watches and serious complications rather than a rapid expansion of references.

items.title: Legare revives an overlooked double-balance idea.
items.summary: The new independent brand’s Chapter I AGP Inverted draws on Albert-Gustave Piguet’s 1932 double-balance chronometer project. Its inverted LC1-AGP-01 movement makes the mechanism the visual centre, showing a different route to distinction than another conventional tourbillon.

items.title: Timex brings the premium GMT down to 38mm.
items.summary: Timex’s Atelier GMT Première M1a reduces the collection to a 38mm case while retaining a Swiss movement and double-domed sapphire crystal. It is a useful sign that the smaller-case trend is reaching a genuinely broad consumer brand, not only high-end houses.

items.title: King Seiko lets Tokyo enter the dial.
items.summary: King Seiko’s new steel Vanac HKF005 uses a dark, speckled dial to evoke Tokyo’s night skyline. It is a regular-production release—not another scarcity exercise—and shows how a familiar sports-watch format can gain character through surface rather than complication.

items.title: Breitling turns a Miles Davis tribute into a collecting proposition.
items.summary: The 500-piece Navitimer B09 Miles Davis draws on the musician’s ref. 806, with a hand-wound chronograph and a reworked Air Racer bracelet. More tellingly, the 50-set top tier includes entry to Breitling’s forthcoming Social Club—an increasingly experiential approach to ownership.

items.title: Awake makes lacquer the point, not the decoration.
items.summary: Awake’s new Son Mai Frosted Leaf colours continue its use of Vietnamese lacquer, natural pigments and silver leaf, with roughly 15 hours of work in each dial. At around 100 pieces per colour each year, it is a useful example of an independent brand building distinction through craft at a relatively accessible level.

items.title: Nomos turns its dials into an atelier
items.summary: Nomos’s made-to-order Twice Unique collection treats five familiar models as canvases for nine artist-led dial designs. Each commission pairs a steel watch with an 18K gold counterpart, favouring handwork and individuality over conventional limited-edition logic.

items.title: The GPHG finalists set the stage for November
items.summary: The 2026 GPHG finalists are now public ahead of the November 7 ceremony. Revised, non-gendered categories and a new jury president signal an awards institution seeking a broader global audience—while giving smaller brands a meaningful stage.

items.title: Rolex sends four unique Daytonas to charity auction
items.summary: Four one-off, season-inspired gem-set Daytonas will be sold separately by Phillips in London on September 28. The proceeds support the Federer Foundation and Re:wild, placing a rare public Rolex project at the intersection of craftsmanship and philanthropy.

items.title: Geneva Watch Days signals a renewed search for volume
items.summary: With 71 brands and nearly 400 new watches, the fair pointed to smaller cases, bolder design and renewed interest in more attainable price points—an industry response to shrinking unit sales and younger buyers.

items.title: Hermès’s watchmaking ambitions meet a perception problem
items.summary: After two decades of investment, Hermès is building real watchmaking scale. Yet its association with Birkin access and weaker resale values shows that technical capability alone does not create collector confidence.

items.title: Watch fairs multiply as the industry looks for new audiences
items.summary: Geneva Watch Days continues to grow, new collector-led fairs are emerging in the US, and MCH Group is preparing Basilia for 2027. Physical shows are becoming places for brands, media and communities to meet—not merely order-taking events.
